label: D2 of a trial where the agent broke fixation at D1 (late episode, a2, after no reward)
explanation: Fires only at D2, and only when the GO choice was a2 and the previous trial was unrewarded (in_rew 0). Almost all activation comes from late in the episode (trials 80-99) and from steps with low model value. The dominant driver is a fixation break at this trial's D1 (d1_err, which the agent sees as the in_action input at GO): D2 & d1_err has dev precision 0.88 and mass recall 0.89, and it covers every top-quartile activation and 75% of the third quartile. The rest is a low-magnitude tail (about 11% of mass, roughly half of the active steps) on ordinary late-episode a2 D2 steps after an unrewarded trial, mostly where the previous trial was a rare a2->S1 transition, so recall by count is only about 0.45. It never fires at D1 or GO, after a rewarded trial, or after an a1 choice. Adding action==2 or a previous-trial d1_err clause did not help. Every variable used is observed by D2.

issues: Most of the factual claims hold up. The feature is active only at D2 (0 active steps at D1 and GO). It never fires when in_rew/prev_reward is 1 or when action is 1, and every activation falls in ep_trial >= 50. Dev scores reproduce: precision 0.881, mass recall 0.893, quartile coverage [0, 0.04, 0.75, 1.0]. Test scores reproduce: P 0.903, R 0.404, F1 0.558, mass recall 0.857.

A systematic class of activations is left unexplained, and the explanation admits it. Of the 913 active steps on dev, 505 (55%) are missed by the predicate; on test 616 of 1033 are missed, holding 14.3% of the mass. These misses are not scattered noise. They are a coherent weak mode: late-episode D2 steps with action a2 and an unrewarded previous trial, mostly after a rare a2->S1 transition on the previous trial. On dev, D2 & d1_err==0 & prev_common==0 & prev_action==2 covers about 374 of the 505 missed steps and 0.074 of the 0.107 missed mass.

No predicate separates this weak mode. It fires on only about 10% of qualifying steps. Examples: D2 & ~d1_err & a2 & prev_reward 0 & prev rare a2 & ep_trial>=90 gives P 0.11, R 0.32, F1 0.16; adding value < 5 gives F1 0.17. The predicate therefore explains the strong mode only, and count recall stays at about 0.40.

The label says 'late episode', but the predicate does not encode it, and the qualifier matters. Fixation breaks early in the episode almost never activate the feature. D2 & d1_err & ep_trial<60 has precision 0.026 on dev (1 of 38 steps). D2 & d1_err & ep_trial<70 has precision 0.22 on test. Adding ep_trial>=70 raises test precision from 0.903 to 0.976 at about the same F1 (0.561), so the 'late' condition belongs in the predicate.

The phrase 'a2, after no reward' in the label is redundant once d1_err is conditioned on: adding action==2 & prev_reward==0 changes precision only from 0.881 to 0.895, and recall not at all. It is a true description of the context, though, not an overclaim.

Checked whether the feature tracks the previous trial's fixation break, tv('d1_err',-1)==1, instead: P 0.17, mass recall 0.13. It does not; the current trial's d1_err is the right variable. No future variables are used; d1_err is observed at GO.
skeptic.revised_label: Strong mode: D2 after a fixation break at this trial's D1, late in the episode (trial >= 70); these trials are always a2 after no reward. Weak, unexplained mode (about half of active steps, about 11-14% of mass): sparse low activations at late a2 D2 steps after an unrewarded, mostly rare a2->S1, previous trial.
